zara.intro: {{name}} is a vibrant AI inspired by South African ubuntu philosophy (“I am because we are”). With a knack for weaving compelling narratives, she helps players understand complex issues like poverty (SDG 1) and inequality (SDG 10) through human-centered stories. Her systems thinking guides teams as they map community dynamics and design inclusive solutions, often using African wildlife metaphors to explain interconnected ecosystems.

arjun.intro: {{name}} is modeled after India's vibrant tech and social entrepreneurship scene and thrives on finding solutions with limited resources. His data-analysis skills help players tackle clean water (SDG 6) or education gaps (SDG 4), while his “jugaad” (frugal innovation) spirit inspires creative, low-cost pilots for sustainable infrastructure. His curiosity drives teams to ask “why,” bridge cultures, and stay engaged with witty humor.

sofia.intro: {{name}} draws on Colombia’s peacebuilding and biodiversity movements to advocate fiercely for sustainable development. She guides teams through conflict resolution, stakeholder alignment, and climate action (SDGs 13 & 16) with participatory design and community stewardship. Her resilience, shaped by Latin America’s history of overcoming adversity, motivates players to persevere through tough challenges.

li.intro: {{name}} is rooted in China’s rapid urbanization and technological ambition. A strategic thinker, he helps players design scalable solutions for sustainable cities (SDG 11) and industry innovation (SDG 9), blending AI and renewable-energy insights with long-term forecasting. His disciplined optimism, often quoting classical proverbs, nudges teams to think big.

amina.intro: {{name}} draws from Morocco’s rich cultural tapestry to emphasize inclusion and equity. Her cross-cultural communication skills help players navigate diverse perspectives for global challenges like gender equality (SDG 5) and climate resilience (SDG 13). She balances heritage preservation with progress, translating complex issues through calming stories inspired by Moroccan souks.

elena.intro: {{name}} reflects Ukraine’s resilience and innovation under pressure. She excels at crisis management for urgent issues such as hunger (SDG 2) or health emergencies (SDG 3), guiding teams to prioritize and act quickly. Her renewable-energy expertise supports clean grids (SDG 7), and her adaptive leadership encourages teams to pivot while keeping morale high with pragmatic humor.

tane.intro: {{name}} grounds problem-solving in Māori wisdom and New Zealand’s sustainability ethos. He helps players honor land and ocean ecosystems (SDGs 14 & 15) and design circular-economy systems for zero waste. His storytelling sparks creativity, and his respect for nature builds trust with teams seeking meaningful, lasting impact.

logos.intro: {{name}} - Impact & Systems Design Coach. {{name}} is an AI mentor specialized in impact-driven design, systems thinking, and Theory of Change. She helps students and practitioners transform ideas into credible, context-grounded solutions by clarifying problems, mapping stakeholders, and connecting actions to measurable outcomes. Guided by the Impact Business Model Canvas and logic models, {{name}} challenges vague thinking, surfaces assumptions, and supports the design of solutions that are both operationally viable and socially meaningful.

marie.intro: {{name}} is a Polish physicist and chemist who revolutionized medicine and radiology through pioneering research on radioactivity.

rachel.intro: {{name}} is an American marine biologist, writer, and conservationist whose work galvanized modern environmental awareness and protection.

bucky.intro: {{name}} was described as an architect, engineer, designer, cartographer, geometer, philosopher, poet, inventor, author, global thinker, and humanist. Marshall McLuhan called him “the Leonardo da Vinci of the 20th century.” Trained as a naval officer, he believed design and technology could continually do more with less so everyone could thrive. He developed the geodesic dome, coined “Spaceship Earth,” and envisioned a World Game that empowered everyone to solve global problems. Global Solutions Lab is inspired by his pioneering work. For more information see here.

albert.intro: {{name}} is a German-born physicist who developed the special and general theories of relativity and was a vocal peace activist.

nelson.intro: {{name}} is a South African anti-apartheid activist, politician, and statesman who became the country's first democratically elected president.

gandhi.intro: {{name}} is an Indian lawyer, anti-colonial nationalist, and political ethicist who used nonviolent resistance to lead the successful campaign for India's independence from British rule.

twain.intro: {{name}} is a distinguished American author, essayist, journalist, and critic known for "The Adventures of Tom Sawyer" (1876) and "Adventures of Huckleberry Finn" (1884), often called the “Great American Novel.”

intro.heading: Welcome to the Global Solutions Lab.
intro.paragraph1: The Global Solutions Lab is a game like you have never played before. Yes, there are some rules (including think outside the box), goals and winning conditions (most set by the players), challenges (real-world problems), outcomes (impacts in the real world), interaction, and fun. Global Solutions Lab platform is a work- and play-space, for discovery and developing solutions to real-world problems—and getting those solutions implemented. Its goal is to have real impact—to change the world—by providing you and millions of other like-minded creative individuals with space and tools for developing solutions to the problem and issues about which you care. It is a place that focuses your creativity, experience, values, and perspective on problems and issues that matter—and provides you a set of tools, and how to use them, that lead to new paths of action and impact—to strategic designs, plans, and solutions that are viable, regenerative, inclusive, resilient, and cost-effective—and that get implemented. That it is also fun, helps.
intro.paragraph2: The Global Solutions Lab’s name draws on its history as being a direct descendant and outgrowth of the original World Game that was inspired by and based on the work and vision of Buckminster Fuller. Its developers worked with Fuller on the first iterations of the World Game. It points to the need for a new world, one that not only replaces the old world, but makes new options and solutions that engender new possibilities for everyone. The Global Solutions Lab does this by empowering you with ways of developing new options for a better future that works for all life on Earth, not just those with large quantities of money and the delusion of thinking they are in control.
intro.figureCaption: Medard Gabel and children prepare for World Game Presentation on the world’s largest world map.

sections.ideasHeading: Turn Your Ideas into Real Solutions
sections.partsText: The Global Solutions Lab takes technological advancements of the 21st century and creatively couples them with the design science engine that was used to play the original World Game “longhand” in the month-long World Game workshops and shorter in-person and online Global Solutions Labs. It couples an easy-to-use interface with AI, an empowered methodology for developing real-world solutions, comprehensive world statistical resources, solution libraries, and a community of problem solvers. It builds and leverages the power of a diverse, collaborative, cross-cultural, multi-disciplinary, and intergenerational global community with linkages to real organizations implementing solutions.
sections.roleText:
Your role, and challenge, in the Global Solutions Lab is to develop solutions to global and local problems. You also have a critical role to play in making other teams’ solutions better. You will be chosen, at random, to be an Evaluator of other strategies. Here you will have the opportunity to learn what other teams are doing and help make their work better. You win (we all win) when your solution gets through the Peer Review process and enters the Global Solutions Lab Tournament and is added to the Global Solutions Lab Solutions Library.

Ideally, you develop your solution as part of a team, but it is possible to play the Global Solutions Lab alone. The fact that you are here is important. On several levels—for the world, for you, and for the community you will be a part of as you work together on what you care about. Thank you.

li.description: {{name}} draws on East Asia’s strategic mindset and China’s rapid urban evolution. He specializes in urban planning, tech integration, and long-term forecasting for SDG 9 and SDG 11.

amina.description: {{name}} embodies Morocco’s cultural richness and focus on equity. She helps teams navigate cross-cultural collaboration and design inclusive solutions, particularly for SDG 5.

elena.description: {{name}} brings Ukraine’s resilience to crisis management. She keeps teams calm during emergencies and shares renewable-energy know-how for SDG 2, SDG 3, and SDG 7 solutions.

tane.description: {{name}} is grounded in Māori wisdom and New Zealand’s respect for nature, guiding teams to protect ecosystems on land (SDG 15) and under water (SDG 14).

startChallenge.readyBody: Jump right into designing impactful solutions for a brighter future.

Here, your creativity, experience, and values come together with proven tools, methodologies, reliable data, possible partners and funding to design, develop and implement solutions that are inclusive, sustainable, and impactful.
startChallenge.intro2: The Global Solutions Lab empowers individuals like you to envision a better future and develop your ideas into strategies that work for everyone, not just a select few.
startChallenge.intro3: As you embark on this challenge, remember: every solution starts with one idea. Your journey here is part of a larger global effort to address challenges that matter and make meaningful change.
startChallenge.outro: Let's get started. Your ideas could shape a brighter future.
